text:
A: Hello! Hi, can you hear me? Sorry, I don't know if it's started.
B: Hi, yeah, I can hear you. I think it's started. I'm Sana.
A: Akosua. Hi, Sana. Oh, I saw your picture, the little school shirts on the airer! I've got the same thing going on behind me, look.
B: Oh yeah! How old's yours?
A: Esi's nine. Year Five. You?
B: Zayan's five. He's in Year One. He's obsessed with dinosaurs. That's his dinosaur on the sofa, he leaves them everywhere.
A: Oh, bless him. Esi was horses at that age. Now it's all, erm, these YouTube girls making slime. Where are you?
B: Luton. Farley Hill. You?
A: Thornton Heath, South London. Near Croydon. So, you know, not that far.
B: Yeah. Erm, do you work, or... sorry, is that okay to ask?
A: No, it's fine. Erm. To be honest I'm between things right now. I was in HR at a housing association for years, and then they did a restructure and that was it, I was out. Eight months ago. So now I'm job hunting, slowly, very slowly. I've got about three tabs open on my laptop right now with jobs I keep meaning to apply for. Sorry, that's a lot. I'm going off topic.
B: No, honestly, that sounds really hard. I'm sorry.
A: Thank you. It's fine, it's fine. My mum lives with us, so she helps with Esi, which is a blessing. What do you do?
B: I'm a kitchen assistant at a primary school. So I do the veg, serve at the hatch, wash up. It's only half nine to half two, term-time, so it fits round Zayan, you know? The money's not great, but I get the holidays with him.
A: Oh, that's perfect for the school run though. That's exactly what I'd want.
B: Yeah. Today it was fish and the kids wouldn't touch it. Literally half of it came back. They all just ate the chips.
A: Esi would be the same! Fish fingers she'll eat. A real piece of fish, no way. My mum cooks proper Ghanaian food for dinner and she still asks for fish fingers.
B: Same! I'll make daal and rice and he's like, can I have pasta? My mum says I was exactly like that.
A: Are you close with your mum?
B: Yeah, she's ten minutes away. She picks him up when my shift runs over. I honestly don't know what I'd do without her. Erm, sorry, I don't know if that makes sense.
A: No, it makes total sense. Same with mine. Her knee's been playing up though, so I'm doing more now. Are you on your own with him then? Sorry, you don't have to answer.
B: No, it's okay. Yeah, it's just me and him. His dad has him most weekends. It's fine, mostly.
A: Esi's dad's in Birmingham. School holidays, mostly. It's... yeah. We'll leave that one.
B: Yeah.
A: What do you do for you, though? Like when he's in bed?
B: Erm, I do henna, actually. For weddings and Eid, family and friends. I've got an Instagram but I never post on it. Everyone says I should do it properly, like as a business.
A: You should! Honestly, people pay good money for that. I do hair, braids, my own and Esi's. Same thing, everyone says I should charge for it.
B: Did you do yours?
A: I did, yeah! Took me nearly a whole Saturday, with Esi moaning in the background.
B: They look really nice.
A: Thank you! Oh, I think that's nearly the time. It's been lovely, Sana, honestly.
B: You too. Good luck with the jobs.
A: Thank you. And post on that Instagram!
